prerequisites: No formal prerequisites. Competencies taught in the modules Theoretical Computer Science and Logic are recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: The students master the specification of formal proof tasks as well as methods, calculi and algorithms of computer-aided proving.
They can use practical proof systems.
They can apply scientific working methods (identifying, formulating, solving problems, training abstraction skills).
They can speak and discuss scientific content orally in front of an audience.

syllabus_topics: Gentzen calculus for propositional logic and predicate logic
Typed logic and type correctness conditions
Synthesis of programs and data types
Implementation of non-standard logics in Jape

assessment_methods.method: Achieving at least 50 percent of points from weekly exercise assignments
Oral presentation of the solution of at least two exercise assignments
Oral examination (individual examination) or written exam

assessment_rules: To receive credit points, students must achieve at least 50% of the points from weekly exercise assignments and orally present the solution to at least two assignments. The final grade is determined by an oral examination or a written exam, graded on a scale of 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Computer Science program.
